title: RA 9266 Foreign Architect and Temporary Permit Gate
subject: Professional Practice

questions.stem: Under the RA 9266 IRR, which description best matches a foreign architect?

options.A: A Filipino architect working for a foreign-owned firm
options.B: An architect not Filipino and not registered and licensed in the Philippines, but licensed in the home country
options.C: Any architect who studied abroad but holds a Philippine PRC card
options.D: A contractor who hires a foreign design consultant

rationale.correct: Section 3, Item 30 defines the foreign architect by non-Filipino/non-Philippine licensure status plus home-country architectural licensure.

distractors.A: Foreign ownership of the firm is not the definition.
distractors.C: Studying abroad does not make a Philippine RLA a foreign architect under this definition.
distractors.D: The contractor relationship is not the statutory definition.

rationale.takeaway: The definition turns on citizenship, Philippine registration/licensure, and home-country licensure.

questions.source_locator: RA 9266 IRR, Section 3, Item 30, PDF p.5.

questions.stem: Before assuming architectural consultant duties on a covered project in the Philippines, what must the foreign national secure under Section 38 of the RA 9266 IRR?

options.B: A special/temporary permit from the Board, subject to Commission approval

rationale.correct: Section 38 requires a special/temporary permit from the Board subject to approval of the Commission before the foreign national assumes the covered duties.

distractors.A: A business permit does not substitute for the professional permit.
distractors.C: A professional organization endorsement is not the Section 38 permit.
distractors.D: A contract may evidence engagement, but it is not the permit gate.

rationale.takeaway: For foreign practice questions, look for the Board permit and Commission approval.

questions.stem: What is the Filipino counterpart in the RA 9266 IRR definition?

options.A: The local architect, partnership, or corporation that must work in association with the foreign architect on a Philippine project
options.B: Any Filipino employee assigned to translate the foreign architect's drawings
options.C: The building official who reviews the permit application
options.D: The project owner who pays the design fee

rationale.correct: Section 3, Item 31 defines the Filipino Counterpart as the local Philippine architect, partnership, or corporation that must work in association with the foreign architect or firm on a project on Philippine soil.

distractors.B: Translation or staff support is not the legal counterpart role.
distractors.C: The building official is a regulator, not the Filipino counterpart.
distractors.D: The owner commissions the project but is not the counterpart defined by the IRR.

rationale.takeaway: Counterpart means local architectural association for the project, not a clerical or ownership role.

questions.source_locator: RA 9266 IRR, Section 3, Item 31, PDF p.5.
